identity.tagline: I build systems that prove what they did — deterministic guardrails around probabilistic models, cost and latency as design axes, and every non-trivial decision backed by evidence.

summary: An engineer who builds systems that prove what they did: production AI, serverless platforms, and developer tooling. My through-line is wrapping probabilistic models (LLMs) in deterministic guardrails — the LLM may explain, but code must decide; treating cost and latency as design axes rather than afterthoughts; and logging every non-trivial decision with its rejected alternatives and a falsifiable 'wrong-if-X' test. As the founder of Valixara, I pursue a single thesis: AI that acts must be able to prove what it did.

keyFigures.label: languages shipped in production: Python · TS · Rust · PHP · Go · SQL

solves.problem: An autonomous coding agent can 'lie' about what it just did on the machine — the commands it ran can never prove the real effect actually happened.
solves.decision: Designed an append-only, SHA-256 hash-chained ledger anchored to observed effects (post-write file hashes, per-run git-HEAD delta) rather than parsed command strings — because a fully-bypassed agent can make the command lie about what it does.
solves.detail: Prototyped in Python then hardened into Rust with unit tests proving tampering is detectable; a 5-band honesty model with an explicit 'opaque' verdict — an effect it can't derive is flagged, never silently marked safe.
solves.outcome: tamper-evident audit as a primitive, not an assertion

solves.problem: A used-electronics buyback agent must discover which specs matter per product, but a free-running LLM will ask impossible questions — a Face-ID question on a Touch-ID phone, fan-noise on a fanless MacBook.
solves.decision: Fused LLM flexibility with deterministic domain truth: the model proposes a per-product schema, then a hand-curated hardware-spec table forbids impossible fields. The LLM may explain — code decides.
solves.detail: LangGraph supervisor + specialist nodes; structured output everywhere with retry/backoff; a real P99 tail-latency investigation (45s = 11.5× P50) driving schema-cache pre-warming and a circuit breaker for external tools.
solves.outcome: only data consistent with hardware reality passes through

solves.problem: A pipeline over real business call audio (noise, cross-talk, variable length) needs STT + diarization + summarization + structured extraction, yet synchronous heavy inference burns idle GPU and collapses under bursty load.
solves.decision: Insourced Whisper + NeMo diarization onto SageMaker async endpoints driven by Lambda — deleting external AI-vendor dependencies (a privacy win when the data carries PII) while paying for GPU only on real execution.
solves.detail: In-context batching (many transcripts per call, Pydantic-array output ≈ 80% fewer prompt tokens) plus content-hash prompt caching; treated the model as untrusted — rejecting transcripts whose timestamp count drifts outside a bounded ratio.
solves.outcome: zero idle GPU, burst-tolerant without provisioned capacity, fewer external vendors

solves.problem: An AI security-review harness easily lets an LLM 'confirm' a finding with no machine-verifiable proof — a verdict set by an LLM's prose is not trustworthy enough to block CI.
solves.decision: The centerpiece is a pure-Python proof gate that recomputes every verdict and discards whatever an LLM set: a SAST static trace alone returns 'unconfirmable' and must escalate to a live PoC; a refutation always beats a confirmation.
solves.detail: Chose LangGraph over CrewAI because a non-LLM decision node was required; kept LLM triage outside the deterministic graph, CONFIRMED-only and default-off; drove cost to a <50k-tokens/scan target by letting scanners do the heavy lifting.
solves.outcome: only findings backed by machine-verifiable proof block CI

solves.problem: Real-time field-sales route scheduling: can a new stop 'fit' between two adjacent appointments, with multiple people editing at once and no double-booking allowed?
solves.decision: Reduced it to a conic-section feasibility constraint: a stop is only suggestable if it falls within the ellipse whose foci are the adjacent events (PA + PB ≤ a configured distance), color-banded by great-circle travel time.
solves.detail: Real-time concurrency over Server-Sent Events with first-writer-wins; a memento pattern for undo/redo across the data model; two-way Google Calendar sync.
solves.outcome: geometrically feasible stop suggestions, no double-booking

solves.problem: Protecting PII in a shared multi-department data lake — tokens must not be join-able across teams, and a real-estate schema must never let owner PII reach the client.
solves.decision: Enforced column-level PII redaction at the data-lake layer, and HMAC pseudonymization scoped by department:field:version so tokens can't be joined across teams; for real estate, designed the schema so owner PII can never reach the client at all.
solves.detail: Privacy is a shape of the architecture, not a filter bolted on: fail-safe auth blocks admin routes on misconfig, and a self-authored production-readiness audit refused to ship while P0 findings remained.
solves.outcome: privacy enforced at the schema layer, not accidentally leakable

projects.name: Accountability Cockpit for Coding Agents
projects.summary: A local-first desktop cockpit that gives an autonomous coding agent verifiable accountability — a tamper-evident index of everything the agent actually did on the machine.
highlights: Designed an append-only, hash-chained action ledger anchored to observed effects (post-write file hashes, per-run git-HEAD delta) rather than parsed command strings — because a fully-bypassed agent can make the command lie
A 5-band honesty model with an explicit 'opaque' verdict: an effect it can't derive is flagged, never silently marked safe
Ships two signed macOS apps from one codebase via build-time tree-shaking; a single git tag triggers CI that builds both

Root-caused a memory blowup to an 8-second re-parse of a 53 MB transcript, fixed with byte-offset bookmarks (RSS held flat); collapsed the git scanner from 5 calls/repo to 2 and parallelized it — ~40 repos went 3s → 150–300ms

projects.name: Project-Intelligence Knowledge Platform
projects.summary: A Project-Intelligence OS: RAG + knowledge graph over enterprise context, answerable in natural language with an immutable audit trail of what the AI did.
highlights: Chose Postgres + pgvector over Neo4j / Pinecone to keep relational and vector data in one store with native joins and $0 infra overhead — logged with the recall threshold that would falsify the choice
Picked HNSW over IVFFlat for incremental inserts without a training step; made the chunk (not the document) the retrieval unit
Origin of the hash-chain primitive later re-implemented in Rust in the Cockpit
